claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches readers how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL code to Pulumi when beneficial, and orchestrate both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
The `pulumi import` CLI command accepts a syntax of the form `pulumi import <type>:<subtype>:<Type> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`.
The `@pulumi/policy` package exports a `PolicyPack` class and a `validateResourceOfType` function.
`validateResourceOfType` can be used with `aws.ec2.Instance` to validate resource-level policies, and the instance resource exposes a `tags` property that can be checked for required tags.
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource exposes an `acl` property that can take values such as `public-read` or `public-read-write`, which a policy can check to prevent public S3 buckets.

The Pulumi Automation API (`@pulumi/pulumi/automation`) exposes a `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` method, and stack objects returned from it support `setConfig`, `up` (with an `onOutput` callback), and expose an `outputs` property on the `up` result.
Pulumi's `ComponentResource` base class is used by extending it and calling `super()` with a type token, name, an empty props object, and options.

The `aws.ecs.TaskDefinition` resource accepts `family`, `networkMode`, `requiresCompatibilities`, `cpu`, `memory`, and `containerDefinitions` properties, and the `aws.ecs.Service` resource accepts `cluster`, `taskDefinition`, `desiredCount`, `launchType`, and `networkConfiguration` properties.

Pulumi supports implementing infrastructure policies (via CrossGuard/Policy as Code) that can enforce required resource tags and prohibit public S3 bucket ACLs, and these policies can work across both Terraform-referenced and native Pulumi-managed resources.
Pulumi's Automation API allows embedding Pulumi programmatically in applications to create or select stacks, configure them, and deploy them dynamically at runtime.

Pulumi component resources can be built to wrap Terraform-referenced infrastructure so that application developers can consume them without needing to know the underlying resources are managed by Terraform.
